newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian blue chips depress stock market.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian blue chips depress stock market.

text.p: Falling blue chips depressed the Nigerian stock market on Monday, forcing the all-share index to close lower, dealers said.
The index fell to 8554.11 from 8585.63 on Friday as investors continued to offload shares in leading companies to take advantage of an increasingly attractive money market, they said.
"Money market rates are rising because many banks are sourcing funds to make refunds to the central bank on recent forex purchases and dealings on basic travelling allowances," one analyst said.
Bank deposits now attract between 5.75 percent and 6.5 percent interest, but bank sources say some would pay up to nine percent.
Traders also said dwindling returns in some blue chips was responsible for the divestment in their shares.
They said Nigerian Bottling Company which closed 35 kobo lower on Monday at 55.00 naira fell because investors were not happy with the Coca-Cola bottler's conservative dividend policy.
"Investors are moving to cheaper stocks which pay better dividends rather than buy the bottling company's stock at 55.00 naira only to receive 71 kobo at the end of the year," one dealer said.
Similar fortunes hit other food sector firms. Union Dicon Salt was down 20 kobo at 51.20 naira and Cadbury was five lower at 36.80 naira.
Monday's losers also included major banking, petroleum and conglomerate shares.
Union Bank and UBA fell 20 kobo apiece to close at 13.30 naira and 11.50 naira, respectively while First Bank closed at 13.50 naira, 10 kobo weaker.
Unipetrol fell 50 kobo to 68.50 naira, followed by consistent loser Agip, down 20 kobo to 20.40 naira.
But Texaco continued to attract investors who hope it will perform better this year than in 1996 when it paid no dividend.
Nestle which posted impressive 1996 result shot up to 46.00 naira, adding 45 kobo.
Among the conglomerates, PZ Industries dropped a kobo to close at 29.19 naira while Franco-Nigerian group CFAO dropped three kobo to 3.45 naira.
